title: Constructible tame Hecke eigensheaves in positive characteristic
main_claim: Let X be a curve of genus at least 2 over the algebraic closure of F_q, and let G be simple and simply connected, satisfying characteristic hypotheses H1–H4. Then for every Zariski-dense geometric l-adic dual-group parameter on X minus x with tame regular-unipotent monodromy, there is a nonzero locally constructible perverse sheaf on Bun_{G,B,x}. Its singular support lies in the parabolic global nilpotent cone, and it carries coherent Hecke eigenisomorphisms (unit, convolution, permutations, fusion). The proof has four stages. First, the GR char-0 unramified eigencomplex on a nodal smoothing. Second, nearby cycles to the twisted node of alcove type, giving the enhanced-flag stack. Third, perverse truncation via Betti spectral frames, then torus descent q_!, using the central-sheaf trace and unipotent boundary monodromy. Fourth, mixed-characteristic nearby cycles from W(k), with nonvanishing by specialization detection.

issues.location: Sec 8, Lemma compact-eigencomplex; Sec 7, eq. descent-local-trace
issues.description: Two essential inputs are used as black boxes. (1) The characteristic-zero restricted l-adic geometric Langlands equivalence (GR Main Thm 1.3.9) together with its compactness preservation. (2) The Dhillon–Taylor free-monodromic central-sheaf trace identity: Tr(m_V) = chi_V in R_T, via the faithful monoidal Wakimoto associated-graded functor. The paper's reduction to these is correct, but the result depends on them in exactly the stated form.

issues.description: In characteristic p, the proof needs generic triviality of the bundle over F'(X) after a finite separable extension of the non-closed field F = k(Z). It gets this by citing Drinfeld–Simpson Thm 2 without checking that theorem's characteristic and semisimplicity hypotheses in this relative setting. The claim is standard and very likely fine.
issues.evidence: geometry.tex: 'By [DrinfeldSimpson, Theorem 2], after a finite separable extension F'/F the bundle is trivial over the generic point of X_{F'}.'

coverage: Read in full: introduction, geometry, detection, specialization, perverse, descent, construction. Foundations: skimmed (nearby-cycle foundations taken on trust). Checks: (a) alcove node-type calculation, root series u^j a(u^n) -> a(t) and u^{n-j}b(u^n) -> t b(t), giving I_B and enhanced flags, with B^- on the second branch; (b) boundary-inverse gluing of the finite torsors and connectedness/density of the lifted parameter; (c) cone-dimension isotropy argument and the general-fiber bound dim(Lambda_D)_d <= n-j; (d) central-cocharacter lemma (p-power Jordan decomposition, root pairing c_alpha, Smith-form spanning of z(m) by central cocharacters); (e) transverse Hecke perfect residue pairing; (f) hypersurface lemma: isolation splitting, exact uv equation, quadric triangle (verified cone cohomology H^{2m} = E^2, odd-quadric cohomology, top hyperplane power = 2); (g) simultaneous-cut incidence triangle and finite-support nearby-cycle contradiction; (h) Psi IC = IC and frame/diagonal exchange induction; (i) adjugate frame lemma (det V trivial so f_V is invariant), localized t-exactness, moving-leg shifts; (j) Koszul unit computation, chi_V(a) = dim V for all V implies a = 1, and H_c^{2r} top-degree nonvanishing spectral-sequence argument; (k) mixed-characteristic parameter lift with l-power root stacks. Not independently verified: GR and DT statements, Nadler–Yun Betti spectral action, Hansen–Scholze exactness.
